title: Service Stewardship: Rotations, Crisis Comms, and Postmortems (2024)
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
> **Archived 2025-03-12:** this page is superseded by "Service Stewardship: Rotations, Crisis Comms, and Postmortem Workflow" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

This handbook collects Redwood's guidance on service stewardship: scheduling and running on-call rotations, fast triage, customer and status communications during incidents, and a learning-focused postmortem process. Audience: primary responders, rotation leads, product owners, and the incident communications group.

Goals
- Lower time-to-ack and time-to-stable for customer-impacting incidents.
- Give every incident phase (detect, contain, restore, notify, learn) a clear owner.
- Keep customer communications consistent and avoid premature technical claims.
- Turn postmortems into tracked action items and keep runbooks current.

Who this applies to
- Engineering responders (SRE, serving runtime, infra, platform)
- Customer Success, for customer comms and severity alignment
- Product and Security, for product decisions and regulatory evidence

Incident lifecycle
1) Signal -> 2) Triage & severity -> 3) Contain & mitigate -> 4) Restore -> 5) Customer & internal comms -> 6) Postmortem & follow-up

Severity definitions
- Sev 1 (Critical): system-wide or multi-region outage affecting >50% of customers; executives notified immediately. Target: page within 3 minutes, bridge in 10 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): major functionality degraded for some customers or a significant error-rate increase. Target: page within 10 minutes, bridge within 30 minutes.
- Sev 3 (Medium): localized degradation with feature impact; on-call handles with async updates.
- Sev 4 (Low): non-customer-impacting alerts, maintenance, noise.

Ownership matrix
| Responsibility | Primary | Secondary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pager handling & triage | Rotation responder | Rotation lead | Ack within target |
| Bridge operator | Rotation lead | Customer Success rep | Sev1/2 bridges |
| Customer status drafts | Customer Success | Rotation lead | Templates below |
| Postmortem lead | Rotation lead | Product owner | Meeting within 72 hours for Sev1/2 |

On-call rotation design
- Rotation length: 1 week is standard for the SRE/serving-runtime primary rotation; 2+ week rotations need manager approval and a backup schedule.
- Handoff: 15-minute overlap for privileged roles (bridge operator, steward).
- Follow-the-sun secondary: primary rotates in-region, secondary sits in the next region for 24h coverage.
- Fairness: at least 4 weeks between hard-week rotations; the rotation lead watches load and arranges swaps.

Creating a rotation entry
1) Add the entry to the oncall-schedule calendar (Team Schedules -> Redwood Oncall) with name, start/end, backup, and contact methods.
2) Put the runbook link in the "runbook_url" field.
3) Notify primary, secondary, and Customer Success in Slack #rotations and by email 72 hours before start.
4) Rotation lead smoke-tests the runbook within 48 hours before start.

Runbook hygiene
Runbooks are validated annually and must contain: overview and owner, signal sources and thresholds, quick triage checklist (top 6 checks with commands), containment steps, restore steps, customer workarounds, test instructions, changelog, last test and next review dates.

Quick triage checklist
1) Confirm the alert: metric/trace-id and time window.
2) Check dependencies (redis, kv-store, model-serving pool) on dashboards.
3) Size the blast radius: services, regions, tenants.
4) Over threshold? Raise severity and open a bridge.
5) Contain short-term (rate limit, feature flag off).
6) Open a thread for follow-ups and evidence.

Bridge & comms
- Rotation lead starts the bridge; primary responder does if the lead is unavailable.
- Bridge header: title, severity, time detected, impact, owner, runbook link, next update ETA.
- Cadence: every 15 minutes for Sev1, every 30 minutes for Sev2 until stable.

Status page template (public)
- Title: [Region] Degraded API latency impacting customers
- Time detected: 2025-02-18T14:21 UTC
- Impact: Higher latency on text-generation endpoints in us-west1; some requests time out and retries may succeed.
- Current status: Investigating; mitigation in progress.
- Next update: 2025-02-18T14:40 UTC

Private customer notice
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference latency (us-west1)
Body: Dear <Customer Name>,
We are investigating elevated latency on text-generation endpoints in us-west1 that may cause some requests to time out. Temporary throttling is in place and a mitigation is rolling out. Our next update will be by <time>. If errors persist, reply here or contact your CSM. We apologize for the disruption.

Escalation and executive notification
- Sev1 sends SMS to on-call, rotation lead, and the Pager Duty exec list.
- Sev1 lasting >30 minutes: rotation lead writes a 4-line exec summary (impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, next steps/ETA).

Postmortem workflow (required for Sev1/2; recommended for Sev3 with >1 tenant impacted)
1) Triage owner posts the initial timeline in the incident doc within 24 hours.
2) Postmortem lead holds the meeting within 72 hours (engineering, product, customer success, security if relevant).
3) Sections: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root cause analysis (5 whys / fishbone), Contributing factors, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Preventative controls.
4) Action items go into the central tracker (Jira project OPS-INC); at least one high/critical action within 2 weeks, the rest triaged into the roadmap.
5) Publish the postmortem to the internal incident archive no later than 14 days after the incident and link it from the runbook.

Postmortem quality rubric (Pass/Fail each)
- Timeline with evidence (logs, traces, metrics)
- Root cause, not just symptoms
- Assigned corrective actions with dates
- Learnings that change runbooks/process
- Stakeholder communication included

Game days
- Each service runs one annually (SRE-organized); critical services twice a year.
- Scenarios: autoscaling failure, network partition, model-serving cold cache.
- Pre-game: runbook smoke-tested, backups verified, participants assigned, comms templates checked.
- Retro: max 3 actions with owners; runbooks updated within 14 days.

Forensics & evidence collection
- Collect sampled request traces, service logs, autoscaler events, kernel metrics, GPU telemetry.
- Retention: keep a compressed evidence bundle for 30 days in the incident bucket, labeled incident-id, severity, service.

Runbook testing cadence
- Weekly automated smoke checks for critical runbooks.
- Quarterly manual validation by the rotation lead.
- Annual full audit by engineering reliability QA.

Customer credits & remediation
- Credits follow the customer SLA policy when monthly availability drops below the contracted SLA; Customer Success owns credit comms.
- Rotation lead documents the mitigation; CSM drafts the message; Legal reviews for enterprise customers when credits are proposed.

Template snippets
Bridge start (Slack):
"[BRIDGE] Sev{level} - {service} - {short-impact} - Bridge: {link} - Owner: @{owner} - Next update: +15m"

Public status update:
"Update: Engineers have identified a partial region-level degradation affecting {service}. Temporary throttling is applied and we are monitoring. No customer data exposure is suspected. Next update in 15 minutes."

Action item example:
- OPS-INC-412: Raise autoscaler cooldown from 30s -> 90s to reduce oscillation. Owner: @alex. ETA: 2025-02-28.

Maintenance
- The eng rotation lead reviews this page annually and after every Sev1/2.
- Runbook changes from postmortems are applied within 14 days and validated by the next rotation.

Appendix: commands and dashboards
- Dashboards: Runtime-Latency, ModelPool-Utilization, Edge-Errors, Redis-Client-Errors
- CLI:
  - curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/v1/ping
  - rtx tail --service serving-runtime --since 5m | jq '.level=="error"'
  - k get hpa -n serving-runtime

Contacts
- Incident mailbox: incidents@redwood.ai
- Pager duty escalation list: pd-sev1@redwood.ai
- Rotation QA: rotations@redwood.ai
